title: Cross-functional changelog sprint and approval rotations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Create a repeatable, tier-aware changelog drafting and stakeholder review process that covers (1) internal exec brief, (2) public customer changelog (tiers: self-serve, enterprise, dedicated), and (3) partner/marketplace notes. Deliverables: a fillable changelog template, an approval rotation schedule, a legal/PII redaction checklist, and a lightweight playbook for embargoed releases and translation handoff. Success metrics: reduce time-to-publish by 40% vs prior releases, zero missed redaction flags in legal review, and >90% on-time stakeholder signoff during the next three releases.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Template is available in Confluence and used for two pilot releases; 2) Approval rotation calendar created and integrated with Slack reminders and shared calendar; 3) Legal/Compliance signs off on redaction checklist and approves the pilot; 4) Postmortem after pilot with action items documented.

notes: Design decision: Use a 3-part structure (TL;DR, What changed, Impact & migrations) with optional deeper technical appendix for infra/dedicated releases.

Distribution channels: Console changelog (short), Public blog post (long-form narrative + examples), Enterprise email (customer-specific notes + upgrade guidance), Partner marketplace blurb (concise).
Fallbacks: If legal signoff misses the window, publish a limited public changelog with technical appendix gated until clearance and notify affected customers via support ticketing.
Metrics to track: time from draft to publish, number of redaction edits requested by Legal, stakeholder signoff latency (median and 95th percentile).
